name: Bicycle
title: Road bike (2×11-speed)
intro: This is a road bike. Tap any part to see what it does, or ask me "How does pedalling turn the rear wheel?"
suggest: How does pedalling turn the rear wheel?
Why does the wheel keep turning when I stop pedalling?
Show me how many more teeth the chainring has than the cassette
looksLike: bicycle, bike, road bike, mountain bike, chain, chainring, derailleur

frame.name: Frame
frame.info: A diamond frame made of front and rear triangles. Triangles resist bending under load, keeping the frame light and stiff.

fork.name: Fork
fork.info: Holds the front wheel and passes through the head tube. Turning the handlebar steers the front wheel through the fork.

stem.name: Stem
stem.info: Clamps the handlebar to the fork. Its length and angle set the reach and height of the bars.

handlebar.name: Handlebar
handlebar.info: Road drop bar: hold the tops to sit upright, or the drops to cut wind drag. Brake and shift levers sit here.

seatpost.name: Seatpost
seatpost.info: Slides inside the seat tube to adjust the saddle height.

saddle.name: Saddle
saddle.info: Supports your sit bones. Its narrow shape lets your thighs pedal freely without rubbing.

front_wheel.name: Front wheel
front_wheel.info: A 700C wheel with hub, spokes, rim and tyre. Pre-tensioned steel spokes support the bike's weight through tension.

rear_wheel.name: Rear wheel
rear_wheel.info: A one-way ratchet inside the rear hub locks when you pedal forward and slips when you stop, letting the bike coast.

crank.name: Crank
crank.info: A 17 cm lever that turns foot force into torque on the chainring. Left and right cranks sit 180° apart.

pedal_l.name: Left pedal
pedal_l.info: Mounted at the end of the crank to take your foot's push as it circles around.

pedal_r.name: Right pedal
pedal_r.info: Mounted at the end of the crank to take your foot's push as it circles around.

chainring.name: Chainring
chainring.info: The 50-tooth front gear. One full turn pulls 50 chain links forward.

chain.name: Chain
chain.info: Transfers power from the front chainring to the rear cassette. The tight top run pulls the load.

cassette.name: Cassette
cassette.info: Rear gear stack (11 to 28 teeth). Smaller sprockets are harder but faster; larger ones make climbing easier.

rear_derailleur.name: Rear derailleur
rear_derailleur.info: Shifts the chain across different cassette sprockets when you press the shifter.

front_derailleur.name: Front derailleur
front_derailleur.info: Moves the chain between the big and small front chainrings for a larger gear jump.

brake_front.name: Front brake
brake_front.info: Pulling the lever tightens the cable, making the caliper pads squeeze the rim and turn kinetic energy into heat.

brake_rear.name: Rear brake
brake_rear.info: Squeezes the rear rim to slow down. Because weight shifts forward under braking, the front brake provides more stopping power.

drives.pedal: Pedalling (crank → chainring → chain → cassette → rear wheel)
drives.coast: Coasting (no pedalling; the ratchet lets the wheel keep turning)

steps.say: Push the pedal and the crank acts as a lever, creating torque to turn the chainring.

quiz.q: When you push the pedal down, what turns first?
options: The crank and chainring
The pedal is fixed to the crank, which is bolted to the chainring, so they turn as one.
The rear wheel
Power must travel through the chain and cassette before reaching the rear wheel.
The front wheel
The front wheel isn't driven; it only rolls because the rear wheel pushes the bike forward.

steps.say: The chainring teeth engage the chain and pull its top run forward.
The chain turns the rear cassette and wheel. With a 50-tooth chainring and 17-tooth sprocket, one pedal turn spins the rear wheel almost three times.

quiz.q: With a 50-tooth chainring and 17-tooth sprocket, one pedal turn spins the rear wheel about how many times?
options: About 3 times
50 ÷ 17 ≈ 2.9. When a large gear drives a small gear, the small gear spins more times.
Once
It would only be 1-to-1 if both gears had the same number of teeth.
Half a turn
A large gear driving a small one increases speed, so it turns more, not less.

steps.say: Stop pedalling and the one-way ratchet in the rear hub slips, letting the wheel spin while the pedals stay still.

quiz.q: When you stop pedalling while coasting, what do the pedals do?
options: Stay still
The one-way ratchet lets the rear wheel spin freely without dragging the cassette and pedals along.
Keep spinning with the wheel
Only fixed-gear bikes without a ratchet do that; normal bikes let you coast.

brake.title: From brake lever to a stop

steps.say: Squeezing the brake lever pulls the steel cable inside the housing.
The cable pulls the caliper arms, pressing the two brake pads against the rim.

quiz.q: Which part of the wheel do these brake pads squeeze?
options: The sides of the rim
Rim brakes press pads against the metal rim's sidewalls to slow the wheel.
The tyre tread
Rubbing the rubber tyre would quickly wear it through; braking happens on the metal rim.
The central hub
Disc brakes clamp a rotor near the hub, whereas this bike uses rim brakes.

steps.say: Friction converts kinetic energy into heat to slow the bike. Weight shifts forward when braking, making the front brake the most effective.

chain_off.title: The chain came off
chain_off.short: You pedal, but the rear wheel won't turn
chain_off.symptom: When you pedal, the crank and chainring spin, but the rear wheel doesn't move. What went wrong?
chain_off.hint: Follow the path: pedal → crank → chainring → ? → cassette → rear wheel. What's not moving after the chainring?
chain_off.observe: Watch the drive train as it pedals: where does the motion stop?
whys: A locked rear brake would also stop the chain and chainring from turning. Look at the chain between the chainring and cassette.
Look at the cassette on the rear wheel—it isn't turning either, meaning no force reaches the back. Look forward toward the chainring.
chain_off.cause: The chain slipped off the chainring, leaving the chainring spinning without pulling the rear cassette.
chain_off.why: Why does the chainring keep spinning while the rear wheel stays still when the chain comes off?
chain_off.answer: The chainring relies on the chain to pull the cassette and rear wheel. Once the chain comes off, the drive path breaks and no force reaches the wheel.
reasons: A dropped chain jams the chainring, stopping the rear wheel too.
The front wheel drives the rear wheel, and dropping the chain stops the front wheel.
